key_insight: Static properties of thermal Gibbs states rigorously limit how quickly quantum information can scramble in SYK and random k-local spin models.
engineering_relevance: The results provide theoretical timescale benchmarks for thermal information spreading in quantum simulations of these models.
method: Analyze the operator-size distribution of the square root of the Gibbs state.
Use this static structure to bound thermal correlators along complex-time analytic-strip edges.
Apply analyticity to constrain scrambling without assuming real-time factorization.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports proofs that, at every fixed positive temperature and with probability tending to one as N grows, scrambling takes at least (1−ε)[β/(2π)] log N for any 0<ε<1.
watch_item: These are asymptotic lower bounds for specific random-model observables, not guarantees of achievable scrambling speeds or finite-device performance.
paper_title: Static Bounds on Thermal Fast Scrambling
